set.perm.order.forced_ask.d: Writes to protected files, untrusted MCP servers, production targets, hosts nobody named
set.perm.order.full: Full access lowers none of the first three layers and does not turn off the sandbox.
set.perm.order.hard_block.d: Safety rules such as deleting system folders or reading key files; Full access does not pass them
set.perm.order.tool_allow.d: Tools set to Allow on the Tools page
set.perm.order.tool_block.d: Tools set to Block on the Tools page, and stored Block rules
set.pz.chatNote: A single chat's own instructions are written in the Instructions panel beside the chat; both apply.
set.sec.mcp.mcp.d: External tools over stdio or HTTP. A trusted server may run the tools it marks read-only without asking; its other tools follow their own setting.
set.sec.memory.trusted.d: When a chat uses a folder, PingDeck reads its AGENTS.md (else CLAUDE.md, first 32 KB) and its folder skills, but only if the folder is trusted. If the file changes, the chat asks again.
set.sec.permissions.rules.d: Left by “Always allow” on an approval. A rule matches only the start of a command and is checked again each time; chained commands and high-risk calls ignore it, and Block always wins.
set.sec.personalization.instructions.d: Every new and existing chat carries this text, before the folder's project instructions and the chat's own instructions.
set.sec.skills.folders.d: PingDeck reads these folders when this page opens, when a chat starts and when you press Rescan, and never changes the files on disk. Each enabled skill is a /name command in chat; to add a command of your own, write a skill.
set.sec.tools.tools.d: These settings apply to every chat; a chat can only make them stricter. Follow mode asks or not according to the chat's permission mode.
